history.dynasty: Welsh Calvinistic Methodist (Presbyterian Church of Wales) mission
history.period: 1846 (congregation founded); present building 1898 after the 1897 earthquake
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. A CHRISTIAN CHURCH — the oldest church in Meghalaya and the 'mother church' of all Presbyterian churches in North East India. Rev. Thomas Jones I (with wife Anne Thomas) of the Welsh Calvinistic Methodist mission arrived at Cherrapunji in 1841, learned Khasi, and is called the father of the Khasi alphabet and founder of Khasi literature. The first converts, Amor and Rujon, were baptized on 8 March 1846 (conducted by Rev. William Lewis), marking the formal establishment of the Nongsawlia Presbyterian Church; the mission had shifted from Saitsohpen to the Nongsawlia property gifted by the Syiem of Hima Sohra, Suba Syiem. The first church building stood on the hillock now occupied by the Nongsawlia Cemetery (est. 1845); it was destroyed in the great earthquake of June 1897 and rebuilt at the present site in 1898. A primary school founded by Thomas Jones in 1843 stands alongside. CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name; real state is MEGHALAYA. (Note: one travel site mislabels it a 'catholic church' — it is Presbyterian; flag.)

name: Nongsawlia Presbyterian Church
town_description: Sohra, better known as Cherrapunji, is a historic plateau town in the East Khasi Hills, famous as one of the wettest places on earth. It was the first British hill station and missionary base in the Khasi Hills, and today draws visitors for its waterfalls, caves and living-root bridges as well as the first Presbyterian church of North East India.
